title: Capacity ops 1:1 micro-plan — forecasting & autoscale asks
content:
Quick scratchpad for Friday 1:1 with Priya (capacity lead). Goal: get directional buy-in on a lightweight autoscale + safety-reservation approach for Q1, surface tradeoffs, and leave with 3 concrete next actions.

Top-line ask
- Proposal: Move from purely reserved-pool commits -> hybrid: maintain baseline reserved GPUs (for SLA-critical routes) + lightweight burst autoscale (spot/ephemeral) with a 15% buffer for single-region failures. Need thumbs up on budget reassignment + go/no-go on trying a 4-week pilot (small subset of customers).

Data snapshot (last 7d) — quick numbers to cite
- Committed GPUs (prod-dedicated): 64 gpus (v100-equivalent accounting).
- Avg pool utilization (prod-weighted): 68% overall; tail peaks up to 92% at 11:00–13:00 PT on weekdays.
- Percent of requests hitting SLO > 200ms: 1.8% public API; 0.6% enterprise routes.
- Cost per GPU-day (effective on reserved): $28; on-demand (cloud ephemeral) approx $42.

Assumptions and quick calc (back-of-envelope)
- If we keep 64 reserved, adding 15% burst headroom = ~9 GPUs. Pilot: route one non-critical enterprise cohort (10% of enterprise throughput) to hit autoscale so we only need ~4–6 ephemeral GPUs during spikes.
- Cost delta for pilot (4 weeks): assume 40 peak-spike-hours/week * 4 GPUs average * $42 = ~$26k. If we save 10% on reserved capacity by rightsizing after pilot, payback in ~3 months.

Key risks to surface
- Cold-start latency for autoscaled nodes — may affect tail SLOs; mitigation: maintain short-lived pre-warmed instances (1–2 nodes) and use container snapshotting.
- Data-handling / tenant isolation for ephemeral instances in private deployments — need SRE sign-off.
- Billing/chargeback complexity for customers on reserved contracts. Legal may need to review pilot T&Cs.

Draft 1:1 agenda (20–30 min)
1) 2 min: goal of this 1:1 (pilot decision + budget ask).
2) 6 min: share numbers above + micro-sim of cost tradeoffs.
3) 8 min: propose configuration (baseline reserved, autoscale policy, prewarm window, canary cohort).
4) 6 min: hit blockers (SRE, legal, console UX) + timeline ask.
5) 3–4 min: agree next steps + owners.

Specific proposal details to land in the meeting
- Baseline reserved: keep 64 GPUs for SLA routes; reclass 6 GPUs as "rightsizing candidates" after pilot.
- Autoscale policy (pilot): scale unit = 1 GPU; cooldown = 120s; max burst = 12 GPUs; prewarm = 2 GPUs for 90s; routing tie-breaker: enterprise tier -> prefer reserved nodes.
- Observability: create temporary dashboard (per-route latency + token cost) and a regression alert (1% increase in SLO misses over baseline triggers rollback).

Questions I want answered in the 1:1
- Is engineering + finance OK with an incremental $26k pilot spend (Q1 contingency)?
- Are we comfortable pilot-ing only on private/dedicated enterprise cohort or should we include hosted API customers?
- Any blocking compliance/legal concerns for ephemeral instance use in customer VPCs?

Follow-ups I want to leave with (owners & deadlines)
- Priya: greenlight pilot budget (yes/no + contingency cap) — due: EOD next Tue.
- Me (Alex): draft detailed pilot runbook + canary cohort list + sample alert thresholds — due: Tue 2 days before pilot.
- SRE (Samir): quick feasibility check on prewarm snapshot and expected cold-start median — due: 48 hours.
- Finance (Maya): advise on how to track pilot spend vs reserved commit amortization (cost center mapping) — due: 1 week.
- Legal: short review of pilot T&Cs if customers included — loop in if Priya says include enterprise customers.

Notes to self / things to say (bullet talking points)
- Emphasize pilot is small, reversible, and instrumented with clear regression alerting.
- We can stage pilot in two waves: (A) internal/QA + non-critical enterprise cohort; (B) expand if no regressions after 2 weeks.
- Highlight that naive autoscale increases cost but may reduce customer-reported latency incidents and reduce need for larger reserved buys.

Open items / TODOs after the call
- Build temporary dashboard: per-route p50/p95/p99 latency, token cost, GPU utilization (per GPU and pool).
- Prepare a short one-pager for GTM to explain pilot (if we include customers).
- Draft a rollback playbook (how to flip off autoscale and re-route traffic to reserved pool quickly).

Slack snippets I might paste in #capacity-ops
- "Planning a 4-week autoscale pilot for a small enterprise cohort. Budget ask ~26k. Prewarm 2 GPUs, max burst 12. Looking for quick SRE feasibility check — @samir_ptl can you confirm cold-start expectations?"

Quick mental checklist before 1:1
- [ ] Bring up sample cost calc and be ready to tweak numbers live.
- [ ] Have 2 options (conservative / aggressive) for max burst.
- [ ] Be explicit about rollback conditions (SLO regression or >2 customer complaints).

Versioning / future notes
- If pilot approved: create a formal doc under shared_drives/engineering/platform-engineering/capacity/pilots/ with runbook and measurement plan.
- If rejected: capture reasons and propose smaller scope (e.g., prewarm-only experiment).

Random thought: consider a small experiment using quantized-model variants for burst lanes (lower GPU memory, lower cost) — could we route less-critical routes to 4-bit variants during spikes? Worth raising as stretch idea if Priya asks about longer-term savings.

End of scratchpad. Will tidy into proper runbook if Priya says yes.
